ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher refund of $6.43 to the rider for the unexcused detour segment (RydeTAXI meter excess kilometres), and remind the driver that a rider's agreement to a short stop does not authorise a route change.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI trip billed on the meter, so the disputed $39.18 is not a fixed quote and extra kilometres flow straight into what the rider paid [F7]; RD-2 therefore requires me to refund the extra_km of any segment that no exemption covers, at this trip's own per-kilometre rate [F4][RD-2].

The trace settles the incident screen: no traffic incident was recorded on the replaced stretch during the window [F14], and the only speed records on the corridor are band 5 (40–49 km/h) in fair weather [F12][F13][F15], so the RD-4 "reasonable cause" exemption fails [RD-4]. There is exactly one off-route segment: 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, +4.56 km, reaching 1958 m from the optimal route [F3]. RD-1 treats that segment as a deviation unless RD-3 or RD-5 excuses it [F3][RD-1].

On RD-3, the stop request came from the driver, not the rider: the "petrol station just ahead" wording is the driver's own description of a place he chose, and the rider's reply "Sure, no problem." names no place at all [F8][F9]. This is not a rider-named stop under RD-3(a) — the rider named nothing, the driver chose the location, so the segment's extra_km is not excused by the stop request [F8][F9][RD-3].

On RD-5, the rider's message at 21:36 does precede the segment start at 21:39, so the timing element is met [F3][F9][RD-5]. But the content is an agreement to a short one-minute stop ("for one minute"), not to a route: in both advocate's readings the ground is scope_other, and they are stipulated on it — a short stop agreed, a 4.56 km, ten-minute loop driven [F3][F8][F9]. The driver's post-trip statement ("I thought a small change of route was fine") is not consent — it was written after the trip and cannot establish agreement (G11) — but it does confirm he treated the stop as licence to change the route, which is exactly the extension the consented scope does not cover [F11][RD-5].

Both sides also agree the loop delivered nothing the rider asked for: the meter records only $0.11 of waiting, 0.4 min, and no petrol stop appears anywhere in the record [F5][F8]. The segment therefore counts, and the arithmetic is common ground between the advocates: the trace's formula is Σ extra_km × ($26.31 ÷ 18.66 km) [F4][F7][RD-2]. $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km; 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4296, i.e. $6.43. The remaining 0.24 km of corridor/matching mileage is part of the fare-excess difference that RD-2 does not refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

The $39.18 total is otherwise composed only of published meter components plus the published $1.47 platform fee, with no surge [F6][F7], and the $0.11 meter waiting unit is a metered item that is not refundable [F5][RD-2], so there is no FARE-1 reduction beyond the segment [F7][FARE-1].

The driver's profile shows 4 disputes in 90 days but 0 route disputes upheld [F17]; RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, so no account flag attaches and the profile cannot be used to decide the case [F17][RD-6]. The rider advocate withdrew the flag request on this basis [F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 21:36 message 'Sure, no problem.' replies to the driver's ask to 'pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute', sent at 21:35 and therefore before the 21:39 segment start [F8][F9][F3]. The words agree to a short stop, not to a route change: the place was the driver's own choice and the rider named nothing [F8][F9], and the driver's post-trip statement confirms he treated the stop as licence for 'a small change of route' [F11]. The agreed scope (a one-minute stop) does not cover the 4.56 km, ten-minute loop, so the segment's extra_km is not exempt and is refundable under RD-2 [F3][F5][RD-3][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The +4.8 km / +35% aggregate [F1] is not itself the refundable measure: RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of unexcused segments, and the single measured segment accounts for 4.56 km of the 4.80 km excess, the rest being corridor/matching mileage that RD-2 does not refund [F1][F3][F4][RD-2]. C1 also goes beyond the stipulation by treating the whole distance gap as the breach.

Accepted as geometry but not as an outcome: the segment's 4.56 km [F3] is refundable only because no exemption applies; the finding is 'counts' under the stipulated scope_other ground, not a bare RD-1 violation [F3][F8][F9][RD-3][RD-5].

Accepted: the rider named no place, so RD-3(a) does not apply and the agreement covers a short stop only [F8][F9][RD-3]. This supports the ruling, and the rider advocate's 'not a rider-named stop' reading is adopted; no rejection of substance, only of its framing as RD-3(b)'s 'far stop' branch, since no stop of any kind was measured.

The reading that the loop was the driver's own errand fails on the record: the fuel need was disclosed and the rider replied 'Sure, no problem.' before the segment began [F8][F9][F3], so the ground is an agreed-but-out-of-scope stop, not a wholly unauthorised driver errand under RD-5's first branch.

The 0.4 min / $0.11 waiting entry [F5] does not by itself prove what the driver did during the ten-minute segment [F3]; the refund does not turn on whether a petrol stop occurred, only on the segment's scope being outside the agreed short stop [F5][F8][F3][RD-3][RD-2].
Withdrawn by the rider advocate and unsupported: RD-6 needs route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1, and the driver's profile shows 0 route disputes upheld [F17][RD-6]. No account flag issues.
The timing point is correct — consent preceded the deviation [F3][F9] — but RD-5 also requires the agreement to cover the segment. It covers a one-minute stop, not a 4.56 km loop [F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

The rider did not name the stopping place; the driver described 'the petrol station just ahead' and chose the location, so RD-3(a) cannot exempt the segment regardless of whether a stop occurred [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

Accepted only as to fare schema: the $39.18 is published meter components plus the $1.47 platform fee with no surge and only $0.11 meter waiting [F5][F6][F7][FARE-1]; it does not answer the RD-2 distance refund, which the driver's own brief concedes at $6.43 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2].
Accepted: the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld, so the RD-6 predicate for a flag_account is absent [F17][RD-6]. No flag is set for either party.

Accepted that the post-trip statement is not rider consent [F11][RD-5]; it is used here only as the driver's own account of extending the stop into a route change, which confirms the scope question rather than creating a different ground [F11][F8][RD-5].
